To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) monocytes are short-lived cells, whereas MΦ and DC are long-lived cells; and 2) HIV-1 can infect monocytes, DC and MΦ, which are important for viral dissemination, but the role of these myeloid cells in HIV persistence is not fully understood.

(1) HIV-1 infection of monocytes, DC and MΦ leads to a dysregulation of their homeostasis and function, (2) HIV-1 infected monocytes and DC are able to transmit the virus to other target cells and (3) HIV-1 persistence in MΦ is still a matter to be clarified.
HIV-1 can persistently infect monocytes and DC in the absence of ART, but the role of these cells in the establishment of viral reservoirs is controversial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of myeloid cell subsets in the development and maintenance of HIV reservoirs and the contribution of these cells to the development of HIV-associated immune activation.
understanding the biology of myeloid cell subsets during HIV infection and their contribution to the establishment, persistence and/or reactivation of viral reservoirs during ART.
the study of the biology of monocyte, DC and macrophages and their implication during HIV pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
myeloid cells, including monocytes, DC and MΦ, are important targets for HIV replication and viral persistence.
myeloid cells are essential for viral replication and dissemination, and therefore represent an attractive therapeutic target.
monocytes, DC and resident MΦ are key players during HIV pathogenesis and that the contribution of myeloid subsets to the development of HIV-1 reservoirs is still an important and unresolved issue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

monocytes and DC play an essential role in the establishment of HIV-1 reservoirs and that MΦ, which are not considered to be a major source of HIV-1 during acute infection, may contribute to viral persistence in ART-treated individuals.
HIV-1 infection of DC is a key event for the establishment of the HIV reservoir in CD4+ cells.
the monocyte and dendritic cell biology is important to understand the pathogenesis of HIV-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monocyte-derived DC and MΦ are the main HIV reservoirs and are responsible for viral dissemination.
HIV-1 infection of monocytes and MΦ is a key component of the viral life cycle and that the persistence of these cells in ART-treated individuals could be a major contributor to viral reservoirs.
the biology of monocyte and DC subsets is highly dependent on the tissue microenvironment.
